What an AI receptionist actually is

An AI receptionist is a voice agent that picks up your business calls, talks with the caller in plain spoken English, and handles the routine part of the conversation the way a front desk person would.

People also call it an artificial intelligence receptionist, a virtual AI receptionist or a voice AI receptionist. The names describe the same thing: a program that hears the caller, decides what the caller is asking for, and answers out loud. What separates a useful one from a frustrating one is not the voice. It is what the agent has been told about your business and what it is allowed to do next.

We set these up for small businesses on HighLevel, and we manage them afterward. You do not get a login and a manual. You get a front desk AI receptionist that has been fed your real hours, your real service list and your rules about who gets which call.

Six jobs it can take off your plate

Each of these is switched on, shaped or left off depending on your business. None of them is automatic until we have configured and tested it with you.

  • GreetingIt answers with your business name and a greeting you approve, at any hour, including the calls that ring while you are on a ladder or with a customer.
  • Answering questionsHours, location, which services you offer, whether you serve a certain town, what to bring to an appointment. It answers from the facts you hand us, not from guesses.
  • Taking messagesWhen a caller needs you personally, it collects the name, the callback number and the reason for the call, and the details reach you after the call ends.
  • BookingIt can offer open times from a calendar you control and put the appointment on it, following the booking rules you set.
  • TransferringWhen a call should go to a person, it can transfer the caller to the number you pick.
  • After-hours coverageNights, weekends and holidays are covered by the same agent, and we write what it should offer then, such as the next open appointment instead of a same-day callback.

One call, start to finish

This is a generic example, not a recording. It shows the order of events on a typical call to a small service business after closing time.

  1. The phone rings and nobody is free. Your number forwards the call to the AI receptionist, so the caller hears a greeting instead of a voicemail beep.
  2. The caller asks a question. Say they want to know whether you are open Saturday. The agent answers from the hours you gave it, including the holiday change you sent last week.
  3. The caller wants an appointment. The agent checks the calendar, offers times that are actually open, and books the one the caller picks.
  4. The caller asks something it was not given. A price for a job nobody has seen, for example. The agent says it cannot quote that, offers to take a message, and collects a callback number.
  5. The call ends and you get the record. A summary and the details land in your email, and the call log keeps the transcript and recording so you can check exactly what was said.

How we build it on HighLevel

HighLevel calls these Voice AI agents. Its help center lays out what goes into one, and our setup follows the same pieces.

Approved business information first. HighLevel's setup guide asks for approved business information for the agent's instructions or its knowledge base before you build. That is the part we spend the most time on with you, because an AI receptionist is only as accurate as what it is given.

A phone number on the platform. The agent answers on a number from HighLevel's phone system (LC Phone) or a connected Twilio number, and your existing line forwards to it.

Working hours and booking hours are separate. HighLevel treats the hours the agent answers calls and the times a calendar will accept bookings as two different settings. That matters: the agent can answer at 2 a.m. without offering a 2 a.m. appointment.

A record of every call. Each entry in the call log can include the caller's number, the summary, the transcript, the recording and the actions the agent took, and a post-call email can send the summary to you.

AI receptionist software, or an AI receptionist service?

There are two ways to get one. You can buy AI receptionist software and set it up yourself: write the instructions, connect the phone number and calendar, test it, and come back to fix it whenever your hours or services change. Plenty of owners do that well. Others would rather not spend their evenings in a settings screen.

Our AI receptionist services are the second way. We are a small agency, and the founder configures each system himself. We write the agent's instructions with you, load the facts, wire up the calendar and the transfers, run practice calls until it answers the way you want, and keep adjusting it month to month. If you search for AI receptionist companies or an AI receptionist agency, that difference is the one to ask every provider about: who does the work after the first week?

Where an AI receptionist should stop

A good setup is clear about its edges. We write those edges into the agent's instructions, and we put them on this page so you know them before you buy.

What it does not do

  • Quote a price for a job nobody has seen
  • Give legal, medical, tax or financial advice, or form an attorney-client relationship
  • Act as a HIPAA compliance program or collect clinical or patient-record detail
  • Promise that every caller will be understood perfectly, especially on a bad connection
  • Connect to your booking, practice or field software until we have confirmed that it can
  • Send text messages before carrier approval clears

Outbound calls follow different rules

Everything on this page is about answering calls that come in. Calling people is another matter. In February 2024 the FCC ruled that calls made with AI-generated voices count as "artificial" under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, which means the consent rules for robocalls apply to them. If you want an agent to place calls, talk with your own attorney about consent first.

Texting is not live yet. Voice works today. Text messages (missed call text back, text reminders and texted review requests) switch on once carrier approval clears; that approval is the A2P 10DLC registration US carriers require for business texting from a regular local number. A text confirmation after a booking or a text alert to you after a call is part of that later switch-on; until then the summary comes by email.

AI receptionist questions, answered plainly

What is an AI receptionist?

An AI receptionist is software that answers phone calls in a natural speaking voice. It listens to the caller, works out what they want, and responds from the information the business has given it: hours, services, service area, booking rules. Depending on how it is configured, it can take a message, book an appointment or transfer the call to a person. It is not a person, and it should never pretend to know something it was not told.

Can an artificial intelligence receptionist transfer a call to a real person?

Yes, if you want it to. HighLevel, the platform we build on, includes a call transfer action that sends the caller to a phone number you choose. We decide with you when that happens: a caller asks for you by name, the matter sounds urgent, or the question is outside what the agent was given. For the calls you do not want transferred, the agent takes a message instead so the caller is not left hanging.

Is there an AI receptionist demo I can call?

Our own main line is the demo. It is answered at every hour by an AI receptionist built on the same platform we use for client lines. Ask it about prices, setup, your industry, or the awkward questions your customers ask. It is the honest way to judge whether you would be comfortable putting one on your number, and it costs nothing to call.

Does a 24/7 AI receptionist work with my existing business number?

Usually, yes. The AI receptionist has its own phone number on the platform, and your current number forwards calls to it, either all the time or only when you do not answer. Your customers keep dialing the number on your truck, your sign and your listings. How forwarding is switched on depends on your phone carrier; the AI answering service page explains the common options.

How much does an AI receptionist cost?

Ours starts at $297 a month for a single AI voice agent. The AI Starter package, $597 a month, adds CRM automation setup, review management, monthly reporting and email support, with setup and training included. Other providers price very differently, by the minute, by the call or by the month, and the AI receptionist cost guide lays out what the market publishes.
